# Hand-written smbtorture subtest stream, fed to scripts/smbtorture_to_junit.py
# in test_compare.py to pin the testcase-name format.  smbtorture prints the
# fully-qualified dotted subtest name after `success:`/`failure:`/`skip:`, so the
# JUnit <testcase name="..."> carries the `smb2.<suite>.` prefix verbatim; the
# section-3 require.txt patterns (`smb2\.create\.`, ...) depend on that prefix.
test: smb2.create.bench-holepunch
success: smb2.create.bench-holepunch
test: smb2.create.mkdir
success: smb2.create.mkdir
test: smb2.create.nulldacl
failure: smb2.create.nulldacl [
  (foo.c:123) create failed: NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED
]
test: smb2.create.async-dup
skip: smb2.create.async-dup
